headline: Google is moving free Gemini app users to its smallest model, Flash-Lite, and adding effort settings that use up a person's usage limit faster.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the cut to Flash-Lite was reported on 3 and 4 Oct; new today are the start date and the effort levels, and The Verge's 6 Oct report differs.
importance_line: What changed is the start date and the new effort settings for a downgrade already reported, which affects free Gemini users first, then AI Plus subscribers who lose the Pro model, and the doubt is that The Verge reported on 6 Oct that free users could still pick all three models.
summary: The Next Web reports, citing Google's Gemini Apps Help page, that from 9 Oct 2026 free Gemini accounts get only Flash-Lite, Google's smallest model, while AI Plus subscribers keep Flash-Lite and Flash but lose Pro and AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers keep all three; 9to5Google first reported the change on 3 Oct 2026 and our 4 Oct edition carried it. New today is that Google is adding low, medium and high effort levels for each model, which its help page says “will also use more of your limit” under the compute-based caps that refresh every five hours up to a weekly total.
notes: Repeat of a story carried on 4 Oct 2026; only the start date and effort levels are new. The Verge (6 Oct) reported that free users could still choose all three models, so timing is unclear.
